summary: Pipeline Denotational Design (PDD) is a design-first methodology for data pipelines: pipelines are composed in a typed algebra (PDA, ~30 operations with contracts) where well-typed compositions are 'grain-correct by construction', with remaining data-dependent obligations emitted as SQL/PySpark verification queries and optional Agda/Lean 4 mechanization. A proprietary toolchain (Claude skills /pdd, /build-ddl, /build-pip, /build-jobs plus a typed PySpark framework) is said to be in enterprise production. The arXiv comment and §8 state the experimental evaluation is in progress; no quantitative results are reported.

claims.claim: Grain, behavioral-class and contract-derivable correctness are established at design time at zero cost, collapsing runtime checks to a single input-boundary check.
claims.evidence: Theorems 3.1, 3.2, 5.1, 6.1-6.6 with proof sketches; full proofs deferred to Appendix A; builds on author's own companion grain-theory paper (arXiv:2601.00995). No independent check; 'zero cost' refers to no data access, not engineering effort.

claims.claim: PDD prevents the defects that agentic coding ships (fan/chasm traps, grain mismatch) better than an agent coding directly from requirements.
claims.evidence: Only an evaluation design (§8: RQ1-RQ7, three arms A/B/C, five case studies, seeded-fault catalog). 'The measurement campaign is in progress and the quantitative results will appear in a later revision' (§8). No data.

claims.claim: PDD-Toolchain is in production use on an enterprise data-engineering program.
claims.evidence: Asserted in §7; deployment figures explicitly 'treated as context, never as measured results'; engine is proprietary, unnamed enterprise.

claims.claim: Mechanized end-to-end in Agda/Lean 4 on a real pipeline.
claims.evidence: Claimed in contributions (PDL, §10) and §6.7; artifact described as 'sanitized' but no repository URL found in the text/signals.

patterns.note: Design/spec-first: human validates a compact formal design, agent compiles it to code; no measured evidence yet.
Type-level checker and optional Agda/Lean proofs for pipeline correctness.
Operation contracts and FOL obligations as structured acceptance criteria, compiled to SQL verification queries.
Pre-verified pipeline patterns instantiated deterministically rather than free-form generation.

methodology.sample: None executed; planned five sanitized production case studies (Table 15).
methodology.baselines: Planned: agent without design (Arm C), ad-hoc hand-written PySpark/SQL, Great Expectations/Deequ. Not run.
methodology.models: Unspecified LLM ('the same LLM'); toolchain uses Claude skills.

standards.peer_review: arXiv preprint; 'extended version of a work-in-progress paper; the experimental evaluation is in progress'
standards.artifacts: Claimed sanitized artifact (designs, evidence documents, generated queries, obligation ledgers, seeded-fault catalog); no URL found; executable framework is proprietary.
standards.preregistration: Evaluation design stated before results (§8), which functions somewhat like a pre-registration, but not registered externally.

biases.detail: 'Correct by construction at zero cost', 'not a proof of concept', 'bugs become unrepresentable' without any measured outcome.
Production use asserted for an unnamed enterprise with a proprietary engine; no measured deployment data.
EDB framework and toolchain are proprietary; only method outputs promised.
Single author designs theory, toolchain, case studies, seeded-fault catalog and planned evaluation; cites own companion theory paper as foundation.
§8.4 Threats to Validity describes mitigations (blind grading, differential testing) as if the study were done, while §8 says it is not.

coi.vendor_products_evaluated: Author's own proprietary PDD-Toolchain, promoted as production-ready; no evaluation.
coi.detail: Not a vendor in the usual sense, but the paper promotes the author's own proprietary toolchain with no independent or even self-run measurement.

verdict_reason: No empirical evaluation: the paper's own comment and §8 state results are pending. Formal theorems rest on proof sketches and the author's own companion paper; production claims are unmeasured. Re-review when the evaluation revision appears.
applicability: Conceptually relevant but not yet evidence. The team's healthcare-education content ingestion across 4+ repos is a data-pipeline problem, and PDD's idea (agent compiles a human-checked typed design; data-dependent obligations become generated verification queries) is a concrete form of spec-driven development for ingestion: specify grain/keys/contracts per ingestion stage and have the harness emit and run validation queries on each repo's outputs. However it targets SQL/PySpark, not Java services; tooling is proprietary and Claude-skill-specific (mixed hosts would need a portable CLI equivalent); and no results show it prevents agent-introduced defects. Treat as a design idea to prototype, not a validated pattern.
